subject: science
title: Launch and diagnostic: observable phenomena
essential_question: How can understanding science and engineering practices help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about observable phenomena, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of observable phenomena.
Check, revise, or improve work about observable phenomena using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about observable phenomena.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “observable phenomena.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Begin with a phenomenon, ask a testable question, develop or use a model, analyze evidence, and revise an explanation or design. Keep the explanation centered on observable phenomena. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about observable phenomena. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of observable phenomena and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about observable phenomena; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of observable phenomena and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about observable phenomena; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for observable phenomena, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for observable phenomena works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of observable phenomena, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking observable phenomena mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use notebook entry, model, data display, claim-evidence-reasoning explanation, and investigation or design performance; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply observable phenomena under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Use household-safe materials only unless a qualified adult approves and supervises the investigation.
Wear appropriate eye/hand protection and stop for heat, sharp tools, unknown substances, fumes, spills, or allergic reactions.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting observable phenomena.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of observable phenomena in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

subject: science
title: Correction and reflection: scientific argument
essential_question: How can understanding integrated science and engineering capstone help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for scientific argument, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of scientific argument.
Check, revise, or improve work about scientific argument using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about scientific argument.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “scientific argument.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Begin with a phenomenon, ask a testable question, develop or use a model, analyze evidence, and revise an explanation or design. Keep the explanation centered on scientific argument. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about scientific argument. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of scientific argument and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about scientific argument; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of scientific argument and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about scientific argument; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for scientific argument, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for scientific argument works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of scientific argument, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking scientific argument mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use notebook entry, model, data display, claim-evidence-reasoning explanation, and investigation or design performance; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply scientific argument under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Use household-safe materials only unless a qualified adult approves and supervises the investigation.
Wear appropriate eye/hand protection and stop for heat, sharp tools, unknown substances, fumes, spills, or allergic reactions.
